STEP 1 - Vessel type: shallow-to-medium bowl (white, curved inner wall visible, food sits below the rim with a visible wall on the right side). Classified as a cereal/oatmeal bowl.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: the bowl looks like a standard cereal bowl, roughly 14-16 cm.
b) Reference cue: the blackberries are about 2.2-2.5 cm across; the bowl spans roughly 6-6.5 berry widths across the rim (about 14-15 cm). Both cues agree.
Final width: 15 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Oatmeal (cooked grain base): capacity of a shallow bowl = 0.2 x 15^3 / 1000 = 0.675 L (675 ml). Porridge fills to about 0.6 of the depth (fill ~0.6), so volume = 675 x 0.6 x 0.6 ≈ 243 ml. Bulk density for grains ~0.8 g/ml gives ≈ 195 g. Since the porridge is a mostly liquid mix, the bulk density is nearer 0.8 for cooked oats: ≈ 195 g.
- Blackberries: count visible ≈ 14, plus about 6 hidden beneath the top layer, so ≈ 20 berries. Each berry ≈ 5 g, so ≈ 100 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the oatmeal base is already counted as the bulk of the volume; no extra layer added.

Totals: oatmeal ≈ 195 g, blackberries ≈ 100 g. (Raspberries in the separate bowl at top left are not part of this vessel and are excluded.)

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Cooked oatmeal (with water/milk, no sugar): ~70 kcal/100 g.
- Blackberries: ~43 kcal/100 g.

Energy: oatmeal 195 × 0.70 ≈ 137 kcal; blackberries 100 × 0.43 ≈ 43 kcal; total ≈ 180 kcal.
